verses.zh: 耶稣出了圣殿，正走的时候，门徒进前来，把殿宇指给他看。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] as Jesus was going out of the temple courts and walking away, his disciples came to show him the temple buildings.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

The Jerusalem temple was widely admired around the world. See Josephus, Ant. 15.11 [15.380-425]; J. W. 5.5 [5.184-227] and Tacitus, History 5.8, who called it “immensely opulent.” Josephus compared it to a beautiful snowcapped mountain.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「你们不是看见这殿宇吗？我实在告诉你们，将来在这里没有一块石头留在石头上，不被拆毁了。」
verses.en: And he said to them,[NOTE:1] “Do you see all these things? I tell you the truth,[NOTE:2] not one stone will be left on another.[NOTE:3] All will be torn down!”[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “answering, he said to them.” The participle ἀποκριθείς (apokritheis) is redundant in English and has not been translated.
Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”
With the statement not one stone will be left on another Jesus predicted the total destruction of the temple, something that did occur in a.d. 70.
Grk “not one stone will be left here on a stone which will not be thrown down.”

verses.zh: 耶稣在橄榄山上坐着，门徒暗暗地来说：「请告诉我们，甚么时候有这些事？你降临和世界的末了有甚么预兆呢？」
verses.en: As[NOTE:1] he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him privately and said, “Tell us, when will these things[NOTE:2] happen? And what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Because the phrase these things is plural, more than the temple’s destruction is in view. The question may presuppose that such a catastrophe signals the end.

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「你们要谨慎，免得有人迷惑你们。
verses.en: Jesus answered them,[NOTE:1] “Watch out[NOTE:2] that no one misleads you.
notes: Grk “answering, Jesus said to them.” This is somewhat redundant and has been simplified in the translation.
Or “Be on guard.”

verses.zh: 因为将来有好些人冒我的名来，说：『我是基督』，并且要迷惑许多人。
verses.en: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’[NOTE:1] and they will mislead many.
notes: Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 1:16.

verses.zh: 你们也要听见打仗和打仗的风声，总不要惊慌；因为这些事是必须有的，只是末期还没有到。
verses.en: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. Make sure that you are not alarmed, for this must happen, but the end is still to come.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “it is not yet the end.”

verses.zh: 民要攻打民，国要攻打国；多处必有饥荒、地震。
verses.en: For nation will rise up in arms[NOTE:1] against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be famines and earthquakes[NOTE:2] in various places.[NOTE:3]
notes: For the translation “rise up in arms” see L&N 55.2.

Most witnesses (C Γ Δ Θ 0102 ƒ1,13 700 1241 1424 M) have “and plagues” (καὶ λοιμοί, kai loimoi) between “famines” (λιμοί, limoi) and “earthquakes” (σεισμοί, seismoi), while others have “plagues and famines and earthquakes” (L W 33 lat). The similarities between λιμοί and λοιμοί could explain how καὶ λοιμοί might have accidentally dropped out, but since the Lukan parallel (Luke 21:11) has both terms (and W lat have the order λοιμοὶ καὶ λιμοί there too, as they do in Matthew), it seems more likely that scribes added the phrase here. The shorter reading does not enjoy overwhelming support ([א] B D 892 sa, and other Greek and versional witnesses), but it is nevertheless significant; coupled with the internal evidence it should be given preference.

verses.zh: 这都是灾难（灾难：原文是生产之难）的起头。
verses.en: All[NOTE:1] these things are the beginning of birth pains.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 那时，人要把你们陷在患难里，也要杀害你们；你们又要为我的名被万民恨恶。
verses.en: “Then they will hand you over to be persecuted and will kill you. You will be hated by all the nations[NOTE:1] because of my name.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “all the Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “nations” or “Gentiles”).

verses.zh: 那时，必有许多人跌倒，也要彼此陷害，彼此恨恶；
verses.en: Then many will be led into sin,[NOTE:1] and they will betray one another and hate one another.
notes: Or “many will fall away.” This could also refer to apostasy.

verses.zh: 且有好些假先知起来，迷惑多人。
verses.en: And many false prophets will appear and deceive[NOTE:1] many,
notes: Or “and lead many astray.”

verses.zh: 只因不法的事增多，许多人的爱心才渐渐冷淡了。
verses.en: and because lawlessness will increase so much, the love of many will grow cold.

verses.zh: 惟有忍耐到底的，必然得救。
verses.en: But the person who endures to the end will be saved.[NOTE:1]
notes: But the person who endures to the end will be saved. Jesus was not claiming here that salvation is by works. He was simply arguing that genuine faith evidences itself in persistence through even the worst of trials.

verses.zh: 这天国的福音要传遍天下，对万民作见证，然后末期才来到。」
verses.en: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached throughout the whole inhabited earth as a testimony to all the nations,[NOTE:1] and then the end will come.
notes: Or “all the Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “nations” or “Gentiles”).

verses.zh: 「你们看见先知但以理所说的『那行毁坏可憎的』站在圣地（读这经的人须要会意）。
verses.en: “So when you see the abomination of desolation[NOTE:1]—spoken about by Daniel the prophet—standing in the holy place” (let the reader understand),[NOTE:2]
notes: The reference to the abomination of desolation is an allusion to Dan 9:27. Though some have seen the fulfillment of Daniel’s prophecy in the actions of Antiochus IV (or a representative of his) in 167 b.c., the words of Jesus seem to indicate that Antiochus was not the final fulfillment, but that there was (from Jesus’ perspective) still another fulfillment yet to come. Some argue that this was realized in a.d. 70, while others claim that it refers specifically to Antichrist and will not be fully realized until the period of the great tribulation at the end of the age (cf. Mark 13:14, 19, 24; Rev 3:10).

This parenthetical comment is generally regarded as a command by the author made directly to the readers, not as part of Jesus’ original speech. For this reason the statement is not placed within quotation marks.

verses.zh: 那时，在犹太的，应当逃到山上；
verses.en: “then those in Judea must flee[NOTE:1] to the mountains.
notes: Fleeing to the mountains is a key OT image: Gen 19:17; Judg 6:2; Isa 15:5; Jer 16:16; Zech 14:5.

verses.zh: 在房上的，不要下来拿家里的东西；
verses.en: The one on the roof[NOTE:1] must not come down[NOTE:2] to take anything out of his house,
notes: On the roof. Most of the roofs in the NT were flat roofs made of pounded dirt, sometimes mixed with lime or stones, supported by heavy wooden beams. They generally had an easy means of access, either a sturdy wooden ladder or stone stairway, sometimes on the outside of the house.
The swiftness and devastation of the judgment will require a swift escape. There will be no time to come down from the roof and pick up anything from inside one’s home.

verses.zh: 在田里的，也不要回去取衣裳。
verses.en: and the one in the field must not turn back to get his cloak.

verses.zh: 当那些日子，怀孕的和奶孩子的有祸了。
verses.en: Woe[NOTE:1] to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing their babies in those days!
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 你们应当祈求，叫你们逃走的时候，不遇见冬天或是安息日。
verses.en: Pray[NOTE:1] that your flight may not be in winter or on a Sabbath.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 因为那时必有大灾难，从世界的起头直到如今，没有这样的灾难，后来也必没有。
verses.en: For then there will be great suffering[NOTE:1] unlike anything that has happened[NOTE:2] from the beginning of the world until now, or ever will happen.
notes: Traditionally, “great tribulation.”

Suffering unlike anything that has happened. Some refer this event to the destruction of Jerusalem in a.d. 70. While the events of a.d. 70 may reflect somewhat the comments Jesus makes here, the reference to the scope and severity of this judgment strongly suggest that much more is in view. Most likely Jesus is referring to the great end-time judgment on Jerusalem in the great tribulation.

verses.zh: 若不减少那日子，凡有血气的总没有一个得救的；只是为选民，那日子必减少了。
verses.en: And if those days had not been cut short, no one would be saved. But for the sake of the elect those days will be cut short.

verses.zh: 那时，若有人对你们说：『基督在这里』，或说：『基督在那里』，你们不要信！
verses.en: Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’[NOTE:1] or ‘There he is!’ do not believe him.
notes: Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 1:16.

verses.zh: 因为假基督、假先知将要起来，显大神迹、大奇事，倘若能行，连选民也就迷惑了。
verses.en: For false messiahs[NOTE:1] and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the elect.
notes: Or “false christs”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

verses.zh: 看哪，我预先告诉你们了。
verses.en: Remember,[NOTE:1] I have told you ahead of time.
notes: Or “Pay attention!” Grk “Behold.”

verses.zh: 若有人对你们说：『看哪，基督在旷野里』，你们不要出去！或说：『看哪，基督在内屋中』，你们不要信！
verses.en: So then, if someone[NOTE:1] says to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’[NOTE:2] do not go out, or ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe him.
notes: Grk “they say.” The third person plural is used here as an indefinite and translated “someone” (ExSyn 402).
Or “in the desert.”

verses.zh: 闪电从东边发出，直照到西边。人子降临也要这样。
verses.en: For just like the lightning[NOTE:1] comes from the east and flashes to the west, so the coming of the Son of Man will be.
notes: The Son of Man’s coming in power will be sudden and obvious like lightning. No one will need to point it out.

verses.zh: 尸首在哪里，鹰也必聚在那里。」
verses.en: Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures[NOTE:1] will gather.[NOTE:2]
notes: The same Greek term can refer to “eagles” or “vultures” (L&N 4.42; BDAG 22 s.v. ἀετός), but in this context it must mean vultures because the gruesome image is one of dead bodies being consumed by scavengers.sn Jesus’ answer is that when the judgment comes, the scenes of death will be obvious and so will the location of the judgment. See also Luke 17:37.
Grk “will be gathered.” The passive construction has been translated as an active one in English.

verses.zh: 「那些日子的灾难一过去，日头就变黑了，月亮也不放光，众星要从天上坠落，天势都要震动。
verses.en: “Immediately[NOTE:1] after the suffering[NOTE:2] of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Traditionally, “tribulation.”

An allusion to Isa 13:10; 34:4 (LXX); Joel 2:10. The heavens were seen as the abode of heavenly forces, so their shaking indicates distress in the spiritual realm. Although some take the powers as a reference to bodies in the heavens (like stars and planets, “the heavenly bodies,” NIV) this is not as likely.

verses.zh: 那时，人子的兆头要显在天上，地上的万族都要哀哭。他们要看见人子，有能力，有大荣耀，驾着天上的云降临。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven,[NOTE:2] and[NOTE:3] all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They[NOTE:4] will see the Son of Man arriving on the clouds of heaven[NOTE:5] with power and great glory.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Or “in the sky”; the Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) may be translated “sky” or “heaven,” depending on the context.
Here τότε (tote, “then”) has not been translated to avoid redundancy in English.
Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
An allusion to Dan 7:13. Here is Jesus returning with full authority to judge.

verses.zh: 他要差遣使者，用号筒的大声，将他的选民，从四方（方：原文是风），从天这边到天那边，都招聚了来。」
verses.en: And he will send his angels with a loud trumpet blast, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven[NOTE:1] to the other.
notes: Or “of the sky”; the Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) may be translated “sky” or “heaven,” depending on the context.

verses.zh: 「你们可以从无花果树学个比方：当树枝发嫩长叶的时候，你们就知道夏天近了。
verses.en: “Learn[NOTE:1] this parable from the fig tree: Whenever its branch becomes tender and puts out its leaves, you know that summer is near.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 这样，你们看见这一切的事，也该知道人子近了，正在门口了。
verses.en: So also you, when you see all these things, know[NOTE:1] that he is near, right at the door.
notes: The verb γινώσκετε (ginōskete, “know”) can be parsed as either present indicative or present imperative. In this context the imperative fits better, since the movement is from analogy (trees and seasons) to the future (the signs of the coming of the kingdom) and since the emphasis is on preparation for this event.

verses.zh: 我实在告诉你们，这世代还没有过去，这些事都要成就。
verses.en: I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] this generation[NOTE:2] will not pass away until all these things take place.
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”

This is one of the hardest verses in the gospels to interpret. Various views exist for what generation means. (1) Some take it as meaning “race” and thus as an assurance that the Jewish race (nation) will not pass away. But it is very questionable that the Greek term γενεά (genea) can have this meaning. Two other options are possible. (2) Generation might mean “this type of generation” and refer to the generation of wicked humanity. Then the point is that humanity will not perish because God will redeem it. Or (3) generation may refer to “the generation that sees the signs of the end” (v. 30), who will also see the end itself. In other words, once the movement to the return of Christ starts, all the events connected with it happen very quickly, in rapid succession.

verses.zh: 天地要废去，我的话却不能废去。」
verses.en: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.[NOTE:1]
notes: The words that Jesus predicts here will never pass away. They are more stable and lasting than creation itself. For this kind of image, see Isa 40:8; 55:10-11.

verses.zh: 「但那日子，那时辰，没有人知道，连天上的使者也不知道，子也不知道，惟独父知道。
verses.en: “But as for that day and hour no one knows it—not even the angels in heaven[NOTE:1]—except the Father alone.
notes: ‡ Some significant witnesses, including early Alexandrian and Western mss (א*,2b B D Θ ƒ13 it vgmss Irlat Hiermss), have the additional words οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός (oude ho huios, “nor the Son”) here (so NA28). Although the shorter reading (which lacks this phrase) is suspect in that it seems to soften the prophetic ignorance of Jesus, the final phrase (“except the Father alone”) already implies this. Further, the parallel in Mark 13:32 has οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός, with almost no witnesses lacking the expression; significantly, Mark does not add “alone” to the Father. It is thus doubtful that the absence of “nor the Son” is due to pious scribal motives. In keeping with Matthew’s general softening of Mark’s harsh statements throughout his Gospel, it is more likely that the absence of “nor the Son” is part of the autographic text of Matthew, being an intentional change on the part of the author. Further, this shorter reading is supported by א2a as well as L W Γ Δ ƒ1 33 565 579 700 1241 1424 M al vg sy co Hiermss. Although the external evidence is not as impressive for the shorter reading, it best explains the rise of the other reading (in particular, how does one account for virtually no mss excising οὐδὲ ὁ υἱός at Mark 13:32 if such an absence here is due to scribal alteration? Although copyists were hardly consistent, for such a theologically significant issue at least some consistency would be expected on the part of a few scribes). Further, although some have claimed that the doubled οὐδέ is “necessary on internal grounds” (Bart D. Ehrman, The Orthodox Corruption of Scripture: The Effect of Early Christological Controversies on the Text of the New Testament [New York: OUP, 1993], 92; see also Daniel J. Harrington, The Gospel of Matthew, SP 1 [Collegeville, MN: Liturgical, 1991], 342: “…the syntax of the sentence (‘neither the angels … but the Father alone’) demands it.”), this is hardly the case. Indeed, apart from one quotation from the LXX, Matthew never elsewhere uses the correlative οὐδέ construction. Thus, on a redactional, intrinsic, and source-critical basis, the shorter reading is to be strongly preferred. See D. B. Wallace, “The Son’s Ignorance in Matthew 24:36: An Exercise in Textual and Redaction Criticism,” Studies on the Text of the New Testament and Early Christianity: Essays in Honour of Michael W. Holmes, ed. Daniel Gurtner, Paul Foster, and Juan Hernández (Leiden: Brill) 182–209.

verses.zh: 挪亚的日子怎样，人子降临也要怎样。
verses.en: For just like the days of Noah[NOTE:1] were, so the coming of the Son of Man will be.
notes: Like the days of Noah, the time of the flood in Gen 6:5-8:22, the judgment will come as a surprise as people live their day to day lives.

verses.zh: 当洪水以前的日子，人照常吃喝嫁娶，直到挪亚进方舟的那日；
verses.en: For in those days before the flood, people[NOTE:1] were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
notes: Grk “they,” but in an indefinite sense, “people.”

verses.zh: 不知不觉洪水来了，把他们全都冲去。人子降临也要这样。
verses.en: And they knew nothing until the flood came and took them all away.[NOTE:1] It will be the same at the coming of the Son of Man.[NOTE:2]
notes: Like the flood that came and took them all away, the coming judgment associated with the Son of Man will condemn many.
Grk “So also will be the coming of the Son of Man.”

verses.zh: 那时，两个人在田里，取去一个，撇下一个。
verses.en: Then there will be two men in the field; one will be taken and one left.[NOTE:1]
notes: There is debate among commentators and scholars over the phrase one will be taken and one left about whether one is taken for judgment or for salvation. If the imagery is patterned after the rescue of Noah from the flood, as some suggest, the ones taken are the saved (as Noah was) and those left behind are judged. The imagery, however, is not directly tied to the identification of the two groups. Its primary purpose in context is to picture the sudden, surprising separation of the righteous and the judged (i.e., condemned) at the return of the Son of Man.

verses.zh: 两个女人推磨，取去一个，撇下一个。
verses.en: There will be two women grinding grain with a mill;[NOTE:1] one will be taken and one left.
notes: According to L&N 46.16, this refers to a hand mill normally operated by two women.

verses.zh: 所以，你们要警醒，因为不知道你们的主是哪一天来到。
verses.en: “Therefore stay alert because you do not know on what day[NOTE:1] your Lord will come.
notes: Most later mss (L 0281 565 579 700 1241 M lat) have here ὥρᾳ (hōra, “hour”) instead of ἡμέρα (hēmera, “day”). Although the merits of this reading could be argued either way, in light of the overwhelming and diverse early support for ἡμέρᾳ (א B C D W Δ Θ ƒ13 33 892 1424, as well as several versions and fathers), the more general term is surely correct.

verses.zh: 家主若知道几更天有贼来，就必警醒，不容人挖透房屋；这是你们所知道的。
verses.en: But understand this: If the owner of the house had known at what time of night the thief[NOTE:1] was coming, he would have been alert and would not have let his house be broken into.
notes: On Jesus’ return pictured as a thief, see 1 Thess 5:2, 4; 2 Pet 3:10; Rev 3:3; 16:15.

verses.zh: 所以，你们也要预备，因为你们想不到的时候，人子就来了。」
verses.en: Therefore you also must be ready because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Jesus made clear that his coming could not be timed, and suggested it would take some time—so long, in fact, that some will not be looking for him any longer (at an hour when you do not expect him).

verses.zh: 「谁是忠心有见识的仆人，为主人所派，管理家里的人，按时分粮给他们呢？
verses.en: “Who then is the faithful and wise slave,[NOTE:1] whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves[NOTE:2] their food at the proper time?
notes: See the note on the word “slave” in 8:9.
Grk “give them.”

verses.zh: 主人来到，看见他这样行，那仆人就有福了。
verses.en: Blessed is that slave whom the master finds at work[NOTE:1] when he comes.
notes: That is, doing his job, doing what he is supposed to be doing.

verses.zh: 我实在告诉你们，主人要派他管理一切所有的。
verses.en: I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] the master[NOTE:2] will put him in charge of all his possessions.
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”
Grk “he”; the referent (the master) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 倘若那恶仆心里说：『我的主人必来得迟』，
verses.en: But if[NOTE:1] that evil slave should say to himself,[NOTE:2] ‘My master is staying away a long time,’
notes: In the Greek text this is a third class condition that for all practical purposes is a hypothetical condition (note the translation of the following verb “should say”).
Grk “should say in his heart.”

verses.zh: 就动手打他的同伴，又和酒醉的人一同吃喝。
verses.en: and he begins to beat his fellow slaves and to eat and drink with drunkards,

verses.zh: 在想不到的日子，不知道的时辰，那仆人的主人要来，
verses.en: then the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not foresee,

verses.zh: 重重地处治他（或译：把他腰斩了），定他和假冒为善的人同罪；在那里必要哀哭切齿了。」
verses.en: and will cut him in two,[NOTE:1] and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
notes: The verb διχοτομέω (dichotomeō) means to cut an object into two parts (L&N 19.19). This is an extremely severe punishment compared to the other two later punishments. To translate it simply as “punish” is too mild. If taken literally this servant is dismembered, although it is possible to view the stated punishment as hyperbole (L&N 38.12).
